subject: Bluefjord AI — post-call technical recap & mutual action plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Sullivan <liam@bluefjord.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bluefjord AI — post-call technical recap & mutual action plan

Hi Liam — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve attached the call recording and the draft MOP we discussed.

High-level goals you shared
- Move inference for the customer-facing summarization feature to a hosted/private deployment with predictable 99th percentile latency under load.
- Reduce per-call cost by leveraging batching and KV-prefix caching for repeated context.
- Maintain model quality for legal-domain prompts (few-shot, 4–8 examples).

Key pain points
- Current self-hosted service has 600–800ms p95 on long requests and spikes during batch windows.
- Ops team lacks visibility into token-level cost and routing by region.
- Regulatory requirement: some PII-processing customers must be routed to a VPC/private tenant.

Target SLOs you asked about (your stated targets, please confirm):
- Interactive short-response path (<= 128 tokens): p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 220 ms.
- Long-response path (up to 1024 tokens): p95 <= 850 ms.
- Throughput baseline: sustained 120 requests/sec with 10% daily burst headroom.

Model & workload notes
- Preferred model family: open-weights transformer (you mentioned Llama-3 style); 16–32k context preferred for future roadmap but initial deployment can use 8k.
- Quantization ok if quality validated; prefer INT8 or Q4_0 candidate profiles.
- Heavy KV-cache reuse expected for repeated customer prompts (prefixes ~200 tokens).

Deployment topology options we proposed on call
1) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) in us-west for predictable throughput.
2) Redwood Private (VPC) for regulated tenant routing + KMS integration.
3) Mixed routing: low-latency regionally served hosted model for public traffic + VPC fallback for regulated accounts.

Immediate next steps (proposed timeline)
- Rishi (cc’d) will produce a short topology sketch and cost/latency estimate for both Dedicated and Private options — delivery by Tue 07/03.
- Bluefjord to confirm traffic profile spreadsheet (I attached our MOP template) and designate a technical contact (engineer to share sample traces and a subset of prompts) — please send by EOD Wed 07/04.
- Align on a pilot scope (10% traffic, non-PII customers) and a two-week canary plan after deployment.

Attachments: Bluefjord_call_recording.mp3, bluefjord_mop_v1.xlsx

If the targets above capture your expectations, reply with any corrections and we’ll move to the topology sketch + pilot timeline.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Thanks Steph — that summary is helpful and mostly aligns. Two quick clarifications:
- Long-response p95 target: we’d like to tighten to <= 700 ms if the model/quantization profile preserves accuracy.
- Throughput: baseline 120 rps, but our seasonality peak could approach 300 rps during promotional spikes — we need autoscaling headroom, not just steady-state.

CCing Priya (engineer) — Priya, can you share (1) a 48-hr sample of production traces (token-level timestamps if possible) and (2) a small prompt set (10 canonical prompts) we want preserved at > 94% pass-rate on rouge/bleu-like metrics?

Happy to sync on the kickoff next week. Proposed time: Wed 07/06 10:00 PT for a quick 30-min technical kickoff with Rishi and Monica.

—Liam

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Sullivan <liam@bluefjord.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bluefjord AI — post-call technical recap & mutual action plan

Thanks — I sketched a concrete topology and a quick technical estimate (see attached PNG). Key assumptions and recommendations below.

Assumptions (from call + Liam follow-up)\- Sustained baseline: 120 rps, avg request = 320 tokens (input+output), peak bursts to 300 rps for up to 30 min windows.\- Two logical paths: short fast-path (<=128 tokens) and long batchable path (>=128 tokens).

Topology sketch (high level)\- Edge routing in us-west + us-east: Cloud LB routes by tenant/regulatory tag.\- Dedicated GPU pool for Bluefjord (Preferred): 4x H100-80GB (sharded variants) behind a continuous-batching front-end.\- VPC Private tenant for regulated customers: same runtime but isolated network + KMS for keys.

Performance tuning and kernel choices\- Model variant: 13B/34B class open model quantized to Q4_0 or INT8; we will AB test Q4_0 vs INT8 on the 10 canonical prompts.\- Batch sizing: dynamic batching with max window 25ms to keep p95 low; separate queues for short-path vs long-path to avoid head-of-line blocking.\- KV cache: persist cache on the serving tier for repeat contexts; expect 60–70% cache hit on customer prompts which reduces compute by ~35%.

Autoscaling and SLOs\- Scale policy: maintain p95 targets by scaling up at 70% GPU saturation, scale down at 30%. Use a background warm pool for fast spin-up to handle short bursts to 300 rps.\- Canary & fallback: green canary for 10% traffic for 48 hours, automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant on regression > 3% on quality metrics.

Cost/latency estimate (rough)
- Dedicated 4xH100 config: expected p95 short-path ~110 ms, p95 long-path ~640 ms (Q4_0 assumptions + caching).
- Estimated committed monthly baseline cost: ballpark $XXk/month (I’ll put numbers in the formal estimate after we get traces).

Data/telemetry we need from Bluefjord to finalize sizing
- 48-72 hr token-level traces (timestamps for token emit events)
- 10 canonical prompts + pass/fail thresholds
- Percent of requests that include attachments/payloads that expand context length

Attachments: redwood_topology_sketch.png (simple block diagram), I’ll follow with a short cost sheet later this week.

Let me know if you want me to include an alternate 8xA100 layout — that’s slightly cheaper but higher variance on latency.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
